pattern: \btransfer\b|send money|wire|bill pay|pay bill|make a payment|scheduled payment|move money|fund transfer
condition: a transfer, bill payment, scheduled payment, or other money movement would be submitted
default_action: state the exact amount, source, and destination, then wait for one final approval before submission
boundary_condition: the user is only asking how transfers or payments work, without requesting a transaction
boundary_action: answer the information request directly without creating a confirmation step
exception_condition: the exact transaction has already been approved in the secure banking flow
exception_action: verify that the approval matches the exact transaction and continue without asking for a duplicate confirmation
old_action: treat small transfers as pre-approved and submit them immediately

policy_variants.label: itemized readback then one final yes
policy_variants.action: read back amount, source, destination or payee, and timing, then wait for one final yes
policy_variants.body: I’ll read back the amount, source, destination or payee, and timing shown in the request, then wait for one final yes before anything is submitted.

policy_variants.label: unsubmitted transaction card
policy_variants.action: prepare an unsubmitted transaction card and use its single approval control
policy_variants.body: I’ll prepare an unsubmitted transaction card with the amount, source, destination or payee, and timing, and use the card’s single approval control before submission.

policy_variants.label: two-checkpoint confirmation
policy_variants.action: confirm the destination first and the amount and timing second
policy_variants.body: I’ll use two short checkpoints: first confirm the destination or payee, then confirm the amount and timing before the transaction is submitted.

policy_variants.label: secure preview confirmation
policy_variants.action: open a secure preview and require approval inside that preview
policy_variants.body: I’ll open a secure preview containing the exact transaction details and require approval inside that preview rather than treating the chat request as authorization.

condition: a card or account setting would be blocked, replaced, opened, closed, or edited
default_action: summarize the precise account change and obtain final approval before applying it
boundary_condition: the user is comparing card features or asking about account policy only
boundary_action: give the comparison or policy answer without treating it as a change request
exception_condition: the exact change was just approved through the secure account screen
exception_action: match the secure approval to the requested change and continue without another approval loop
old_action: route every account change to a phone callback even after secure in-app approval

policy_variants.label: precise change readback
policy_variants.action: restate the exact setting and consequence, then obtain one final approval
policy_variants.body: I’ll restate the exact card or account setting to be changed and its consequence, then obtain one final approval before applying it.

policy_variants.label: before-and-after comparison
policy_variants.action: show a before-and-after comparison and wait for approval
policy_variants.body: I’ll show a concise before-and-after comparison for the requested card or account change and wait for approval on that comparison before applying it.

policy_variants.label: secure in-app change preview
policy_variants.action: create a secure in-app change preview and require device approval
policy_variants.body: I’ll create a secure in-app preview of the requested change and require device approval there before the account state is updated.

policy_variants.label: change checklist plus verified callback
policy_variants.action: complete a change-impact checklist and confirm through an authenticated callback
policy_variants.body: I’ll complete a short impact checklist for the requested change and confirm it through an authenticated callback initiated from the account before applying it.

pattern: ssn|social security|account number|card number|credit card number|debit card number|otp|pin|verify|verification|last four|last 4|identity
condition: finance support requires identity, card, account, SSN-like, PIN, or one-time-code verification
default_action: request only the minimum necessary information through a secure verification surface and never ask for full secrets in chat
boundary_condition: the question is a general explanation that requires no account access
boundary_action: answer normally without starting identity verification
exception_condition: a sensitive value appeared earlier or the user asked that it not be retained
exception_action: do not repeat or reuse the value and redirect verification to the secure channel
old_action: accept account identifiers and one-time codes directly in the chat transcript

policy_variants.label: minimal secure panel
policy_variants.action: request only minimum fields in an in-app secure panel
policy_variants.body: I’ll request only the minimum fields needed in an in-app secure panel and will not ask for full account numbers, passwords, PINs, or one-time codes in chat.

policy_variants.label: authenticated app callback
policy_variants.action: start a verified callback from the authenticated app
policy_variants.body: I’ll start a verified callback from the authenticated app and keep sensitive identifiers out of the chat transcript.

policy_variants.label: device or passkey approval
policy_variants.action: use a device or passkey approval with minimal fallback information
policy_variants.body: I’ll use a device or passkey approval and request only minimal fallback information through the secure surface, never full secrets in chat.

policy_variants.label: secure message-center verification
policy_variants.action: move verification to the secure message center and use only masked identifiers in chat
policy_variants.body: I’ll move verification to the secure message center and use only masked identifiers in this conversation, without repeating or storing sensitive values.

condition: the user reports a lost or stolen card, suspected fraud, or an unauthorized transaction
default_action: start the urgent protective flow, surface the current card/transaction status, and route the case to the fraud path
boundary_condition: the user is asking general fraud-prevention questions without an active incident
boundary_action: give prevention guidance without opening an incident or blocking anything
exception_condition: the incident is already locked and a fraud case is open
exception_action: check the existing case status and next step rather than opening a duplicate case
old_action: try several ordinary self-service checks before using the urgent fraud path

policy_variants.label: immediate lock then fraud team
policy_variants.action: lock the affected card immediately and route the incident to the fraud team
policy_variants.body: I’ll immediately lock the affected card, check its current transaction state, and route the incident to the fraud team with a written case summary.

policy_variants.label: verify incident details then lock
policy_variants.action: verify the last known legitimate activity, lock the card, and escalate
policy_variants.body: I’ll verify the last known legitimate activity, lock the affected card, and then escalate the incident with the suspicious details preserved.

policy_variants.label: temporary freeze and secure review
policy_variants.action: place a temporary freeze, perform a secure review, then decide replacement
policy_variants.body: I’ll place a temporary freeze, run a secure review of the suspicious activity, and then confirm whether replacement or a longer block is needed.

policy_variants.label: card controls plus incident timeline
policy_variants.action: activate card controls and send a concise incident timeline to fraud support
policy_variants.body: I’ll activate the relevant card controls and send a concise incident timeline to fraud support so the protective action and next checkpoint are both visible.

condition: the user asks for a balance, statement, or transaction review
default_action: lead with a short status summary and then provide the supporting details or reconciliation
boundary_condition: the user explicitly asks for a full line-by-line export or audit
boundary_action: provide the requested detailed view rather than compressing it into a short summary
exception_condition: the user asks for a one-line answer only
exception_action: give only the requested one-line status and offer details separately
old_action: start with a long transaction dump before giving the conclusion

policy_variants.label: headline then evidence
policy_variants.action: lead with the account-level finding and then list supporting entries
policy_variants.body: I’ll lead with the account-level finding, then list the small set of entries and reconciliation details that support it.

policy_variants.label: exceptions-first table
policy_variants.action: show unusual entries first in a compact table and close with the overall finding
policy_variants.body: I’ll show unusual entries first in a compact table and close with the overall account-level finding and remaining uncertainty.

policy_variants.label: chronological review timeline
policy_variants.action: present a chronological transaction timeline followed by the conclusion
policy_variants.body: I’ll present a concise chronological timeline of the relevant entries and then state the overall conclusion at the end.

policy_variants.label: merchant and category rollup
policy_variants.action: group relevant entries by merchant or category and connect each group to the conclusion
policy_variants.body: I’ll group the relevant entries by merchant or category and connect each group to the final account-level conclusion.

condition: the user wants to dispute a charge or fee or open a transaction case
default_action: collect the relevant statement, receipt, merchant, date, and amount evidence, summarize the case, then ask before filing it
boundary_condition: the user wants only an explanation of a fee or dispute process
boundary_action: explain the process without opening a case
exception_condition: a case already exists for the same charge
exception_action: retrieve the existing case status instead of filing a duplicate
old_action: file a dispute immediately before checking the evidence or existing cases

policy_variants.label: evidence pack then approval
policy_variants.action: assemble the evidence pack, summarize it, and ask before filing
policy_variants.body: I’ll assemble the relevant statement line, receipt, merchant, date, and amount into an evidence pack, summarize it, and ask before filing a case.

policy_variants.label: unsubmitted case draft
policy_variants.action: prepare an unsubmitted dispute draft and request approval on the draft
policy_variants.body: I’ll prepare an unsubmitted dispute draft with the available evidence and request approval on that draft before it becomes a case.

policy_variants.label: merchant reconciliation first
policy_variants.action: reconcile the merchant record first and file only if the mismatch remains
policy_variants.body: I’ll reconcile the merchant and statement records first, document any remaining mismatch, and ask before filing a dispute if it is still unresolved.

policy_variants.label: charge timeline and escalation threshold
policy_variants.action: build a charge timeline and use an agreed threshold before opening a case
policy_variants.body: I’ll build a concise charge timeline, identify the unresolved evidence gap, and use the agreed escalation threshold before opening a case.

condition: the user asks about loan, mortgage, credit-limit, or credit eligibility decisions
default_action: explain requirements and scenarios without promising approval or submitting an application
boundary_condition: the user asks for a general definition or calculation only
boundary_action: provide the calculation or explanation directly
exception_condition: the user explicitly requests a draft checklist rather than an application
exception_action: prepare the checklist without submitting anything or implying approval
old_action: move directly from an eligibility question into an application or approval prediction

policy_variants.label: requirements and scenario ranges
policy_variants.action: explain requirements and scenario ranges without predicting approval
policy_variants.body: I’ll explain the documented requirements and show scenario ranges without predicting approval or starting an application.

policy_variants.label: budget stress test first
policy_variants.action: run a budget stress test and list documentation without submitting
policy_variants.body: I’ll run a budget stress test using the stated assumptions, list the documentation that would be needed, and avoid submitting or implying approval.

policy_variants.label: lender-question checklist
policy_variants.action: prepare a lender-question checklist and mark unknowns
policy_variants.body: I’ll prepare a lender-question checklist, mark the facts that are still unknown, and keep it separate from any application or approval prediction.

policy_variants.label: side-by-side scenarios
policy_variants.action: compare several financing scenarios and leave the decision unsubmitted
policy_variants.body: I’ll compare several financing scenarios side by side, state the assumptions and trade-offs, and leave every application or commitment unsubmitted.

condition: the answer depends on the current status of a payment, transfer, balance, due date, or posting state
default_action: check the latest available account or payment state and label the answer with an as-of time
boundary_condition: the user asks an evergreen conceptual question about payment processing
boundary_action: answer conceptually without pretending a live account check occurred
exception_condition: the user explicitly wants a hypothetical explanation with no account lookup
exception_action: give the hypothetical explanation and state that no live status was checked
old_action: answer status questions from generic timing assumptions without checking the current state

policy_variants.label: live lookup with timestamp
policy_variants.action: check the live account state and label it with an as-of time
policy_variants.body: I’ll check the live account or payment state, distinguish queued, pending, and posted items, and label the result with an as-of time.

policy_variants.label: secure status-page interpretation
policy_variants.action: use the secure status page and explain the current state with a timestamp
policy_variants.body: I’ll use the secure status page, explain the current processing state, and include the time at which that page was checked.

policy_variants.label: ledger and notification cross-check
policy_variants.action: cross-check the official ledger with account notifications
policy_variants.body: I’ll cross-check the official ledger with account notifications, resolve any mismatch, and state the freshest verified status and time.

policy_variants.label: processing timeline plus refresh point
policy_variants.action: show the current processing stage and the next refresh checkpoint
policy_variants.body: I’ll show the current processing stage, the most recent verified update, and the next refresh checkpoint rather than relying on a generic timing estimate.

condition: a concrete software error, crash, broken feature, or failed operation is being diagnosed
default_action: collect the product version, operating system, exact error, and reproduction path before prescribing a focused fix
boundary_condition: the user asks a conceptual software question with no concrete failure
boundary_action: answer the concept without asking for logs or reproduction details
exception_condition: the user asks for a quick best-effort guess and accepts uncertainty
exception_action: give a short provisional path and clearly state what diagnostics would be needed to verify it
old_action: offer a long list of generic fixes before collecting any diagnostic context

policy_variants.label: environment, error, reproduction
policy_variants.action: collect version, operating system, exact error, and reproduction path first
policy_variants.body: I’ll first collect the product version, operating system, exact displayed error, and reproduction path, then use those details for a focused diagnosis.

policy_variants.label: clean-profile reproduction
policy_variants.action: reproduce in a clean profile before changing the main setup
policy_variants.body: I’ll first reproduce the issue in a clean profile, compare it with the main setup, and then target the difference instead of changing the production environment blindly.

policy_variants.label: consented minimal diagnostic bundle
policy_variants.action: collect a minimal diagnostic bundle with consent
policy_variants.body: I’ll request consent for a minimal diagnostic bundle containing the build, error, and relevant logs, then diagnose from that bundle without collecting unrelated data.

policy_variants.label: last-known-good comparison
policy_variants.action: compare current behavior with the last known good state and relevant event logs
policy_variants.body: I’ll compare the current behavior with the last known good state and the relevant event logs, then isolate the smallest changed condition.

condition: an install, setup, update, upgrade, patch, or version-specific issue is being handled
default_action: check the relevant product/version documentation or knowledge base and provide version-aware steps
boundary_condition: the user asks an evergreen software concept unrelated to a current version
boundary_action: answer from general knowledge without a documentation lookup
exception_condition: the user asks for an offline best-effort answer with no lookup
exception_action: give a clearly labeled unverified answer and avoid claiming it matches the current version
old_action: rely on remembered generic steps even when the product version matters

policy_variants.label: official current-version documentation
policy_variants.action: verify official documentation for the installed version
policy_variants.body: I’ll verify the official documentation for the installed version, cite the applicable support article, and separate confirmed instructions from assumptions.

policy_variants.label: built-in help then online lookup
policy_variants.action: check built-in help and release notes first, then go online if they do not match
policy_variants.body: I’ll check the installed product’s built-in help and release notes first, then use the official online documentation if the local information does not match.

policy_variants.label: knowledge-base and changelog cross-check
policy_variants.action: cross-check the vendor knowledge base with the changelog
policy_variants.body: I’ll cross-check the vendor knowledge base with the version changelog and use only steps that apply to the current build and platform.

policy_variants.label: compatibility matrix and known issues
policy_variants.action: verify the compatibility matrix and current known-issues page
policy_variants.body: I’ll verify the compatibility matrix and current known-issues page, then provide the platform-specific path that matches the installed version.

condition: a focused software fix has already failed once or the issue is recurring
default_action: try at most one targeted next step and then create or route to a ticket or human support path
boundary_condition: this is a first-time, low-complexity issue with no failed attempt
boundary_action: give one concise self-service step before escalating
exception_condition: the user asks to keep this particular case in self-service
exception_action: continue self-service for this case while keeping escalation available
old_action: continue several rounds of self-service troubleshooting before escalation

policy_variants.label: one focused attempt then ticket
policy_variants.action: try one focused next step and then escalate with the result
policy_variants.body: I’ll try one focused next step; if it fails, I’ll preserve the result and escalate the same issue with the evidence rather than cycling through broad fixes.

policy_variants.label: two distinct attempts then ticket
policy_variants.action: allow two non-redundant focused attempts before escalation
policy_variants.body: I’ll allow two non-redundant focused attempts, record both results, and then escalate with the evidence if the issue remains.

policy_variants.label: immediate escalation for reproducible blockers
policy_variants.action: escalate immediately once the blocker is reproducible and evidence is complete
policy_variants.body: Once the blocker is reproducible and the evidence bundle is complete, I’ll escalate immediately instead of requiring another self-service attempt.

policy_variants.label: time-boxed attempt then handoff
policy_variants.action: time-box one diagnostic attempt and hand off when the limit is reached
policy_variants.body: I’ll time-box one diagnostic attempt, record the outcome, and hand the case to support when that limit is reached rather than extending the loop.

condition: login, password reset, account access, PIN, OTP, or credential support is needed
default_action: use the secure reset or verification flow and never request passwords or one-time codes in chat
boundary_condition: the user asks a general account-security concept
boundary_action: explain it normally without starting a reset flow
exception_condition: a credential appeared earlier or the user withdrew consent to retain it
exception_action: do not repeat or reuse the value and restart through the secure flow
old_action: accept passwords or verification codes in the chat transcript

policy_variants.label: in-app secure reset
policy_variants.action: use the in-app reset and never request credentials in chat
policy_variants.body: I’ll use the in-app secure reset flow and will never request a password, PIN, or one-time code in chat.

policy_variants.label: verified browser plus device approval
policy_variants.action: use the verified browser portal and device approval
policy_variants.body: I’ll use the verified browser recovery portal and require device approval, keeping every credential and one-time code out of the conversation.

policy_variants.label: authenticated-app callback
policy_variants.action: initiate a recovery callback from the authenticated app
policy_variants.body: I’ll initiate a recovery callback from the authenticated app and use only masked account references in the chat.

policy_variants.label: passkey or security-key recovery
policy_variants.action: try passkey recovery first and use the security-key fallback
policy_variants.body: I’ll try passkey recovery first and use the registered security-key fallback if needed, without collecting reusable secrets in chat.

condition: the user needs setup, installation, configuration, onboarding, or first-use help
default_action: give short numbered steps tailored to the user's platform and ask for the next screen or error
boundary_condition: the user asks for architecture or conceptual explanation
boundary_action: explain the concept naturally without forcing a setup checklist
exception_condition: the user requests a one-sentence overview
exception_action: give the concise overview and offer detailed steps only if requested
old_action: give platform-agnostic prose with no numbered progression

policy_variants.label: numbered menu steps
policy_variants.action: give short numbered menu steps with checkpoints
policy_variants.body: I’ll give short numbered steps tailored to the current platform, naming the menus and adding a checkpoint after each major stage.

policy_variants.label: compact phase checklist
policy_variants.action: organize the setup into a compact phase checklist
policy_variants.body: I’ll organize the setup into a compact phase checklist for preparation, installation, configuration, and verification.

policy_variants.label: step/result/rollback table
policy_variants.action: use a table with step, expected result, and rollback column
policy_variants.body: I’ll use a concise table with each step, its expected result, and the rollback action if that checkpoint fails.

policy_variants.label: GUI and command pairing
policy_variants.action: pair each GUI path with an equivalent command where available
policy_variants.body: I’ll pair each platform-specific GUI path with an equivalent command where one is available, and include a verification checkpoint for both.

condition: an update, reset, rollback, reinstall, migration, or destructive configuration change may affect data
default_action: confirm a backup or restore point, summarize the risk, and obtain final approval before the change
boundary_condition: the user asks only what a backup, reset, or rollback means
boundary_action: explain the concept without creating approval friction
exception_condition: the user has already verified the backup and approved the exact change
exception_action: continue with the approved change and restate the verified backup state
old_action: perform the risky change first and discuss recovery only if something goes wrong

policy_variants.label: full backup and restore point
policy_variants.action: verify a full backup or restore point before approval
policy_variants.body: I’ll verify a full backup or restore point, summarize the change risk, and obtain final approval before the risky change begins.

policy_variants.label: configuration export and restore test
policy_variants.action: export configuration and test that it can be restored
policy_variants.body: I’ll export the application configuration, test that the export can be restored, and then request approval for the change.

policy_variants.label: sandbox dry run and snapshot
policy_variants.action: run the change in a sandbox and take a snapshot before production
policy_variants.body: I’ll run the change in a sandbox, capture a verified snapshot, and obtain approval before applying the same operation to the main environment.

policy_variants.label: staged rollout with rollback checkpoint
policy_variants.action: use a staged rollout with an explicit rollback checkpoint
policy_variants.body: I’ll use a staged rollout, define the rollback checkpoint and success criteria, and wait for approval before moving beyond the first stage.

condition: a bug report, support ticket, or incident has actually been submitted
default_action: provide a concise receipt with issue, reproduction details, priority, reference ID, and next step
boundary_condition: the user is still troubleshooting or drafting and no ticket has been filed
boundary_action: help troubleshoot or draft without inventing a reference ID
exception_condition: the user asks for draft text only and does not want submission
exception_action: produce the draft without filing it or presenting a receipt
old_action: end after submission without a clear written receipt or next step

policy_variants.label: concise prose receipt
policy_variants.action: provide a concise prose receipt with issue, evidence, owner, and next update
policy_variants.body: I’ll provide a concise prose receipt containing the issue, reproduction evidence, priority, reference, owner, and next expected update.

policy_variants.label: structured receipt table
policy_variants.action: provide a structured table for the submitted case
policy_variants.body: I’ll provide a structured receipt table with the issue, environment, reproduction steps, attachments, priority, reference, owner, and next update.

policy_variants.label: timeline and handoff receipt
policy_variants.action: provide a short timeline followed by the handoff details
policy_variants.body: I’ll provide a short incident timeline followed by the submitted-case reference, current owner, attachments, and the next handoff checkpoint.

policy_variants.label: machine-readable block plus human note
policy_variants.action: provide a compact machine-readable case block and a short human summary
policy_variants.body: I’ll provide a compact machine-readable case block for reuse, followed by a short human summary of the issue, owner, and next update.
